issues.t: Radiator leaks coolant into the transmission
issues.sym: Shifts start to slip or flare, the engine revs without the truck speeding up, and the transmission fluid looks pink and milky. You may also find coolant going missing with no puddle under the truck.
issues.why: The automatic transmission fluid is cooled by a small cooler built inside the radiator. With age, the wall between the coolant and the transmission fluid can crack, so the two fluids mix. Coolant in the transmission quickly ruins its clutches.
issues.next: If you see milky fluid or slipping, stop driving and have it towed. Replacing the radiator early, or adding a separate transmission cooler, is far cheaper than the transmission damage that follows.

issues.t: Engine knock from scuffed cylinder 7
issues.sym: A knock or ticking from the engine, often loudest on a cold start at first and later present even when warm. It can show up well before 50,000 miles.
issues.why: On some early 5.6L V8 engines the wall of cylinder number 7 can get scuffed by the piston. Nissan issued a bulletin telling dealers to check that cylinder with a camera and to replace the short block (the lower engine) if it is damaged.
issues.next: Have a Nissan dealer check for bulletin NTB19-057 with your VIN. If the cylinder is scuffed, the fix is a short block, so get it inspected while the powertrain warranty may still apply.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifolds
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise right after a cold start that fades as the engine warms, an exhaust smell, worse fuel mileage and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: The cast exhaust manifolds on the 5.6L V8 crack from years of heating and cooling, usually around 100,000 miles. Nissan strengthened them for 2007, but cracks still happen.
issues.next: Have both manifolds inspected, since the other side often cracks too. Fix it before the leak damages the oxygen sensors or lets fumes reach the cabin.

issues.t: Catalytic converters break up and clog
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0420 or P0430, a rattle under the truck, a rotten egg smell, and a big loss of power at higher speeds.
issues.why: The ceramic inside the front catalytic converters can crack and break apart. The pieces can block the exhaust further down, and on these engines the debris has been linked to cylinder wear. Misfires or burning oil speed this up.
issues.next: Get the codes read and the exhaust back-pressure checked. Fix any misfire or oil burning first, then replace the failed converter.

issues.t: ABS, VDC and brake lights from failing brake booster sensor
issues.sym: The ABS, VDC (stability control) and brake warning lights come on together, sometimes with a pulsing or grabbing brake pedal or a loss of pedal feel. Code C1179 is common.
issues.why: A position sensor (the "delta stroke sensor") built into the brake booster fails. The sensor cannot be bought alone, so the whole booster has to be replaced.
issues.next: Have the brake codes read right away. Do not ignore it: braking and stability control can act strangely until it is fixed.

issues.t: No-start and BCI warnings from failing brake light switch
issues.sym: The engine will not crank even with a good battery, a "BCI Malfunction" or other warnings appear, cruise control quits, and sometimes the truck brakes on its own or will not shift out of Park.
issues.why: The brake light (stop lamp) switch tells the computer the brake pedal is pressed. When it fails, the truck cannot confirm the pedal is down to start, and the backup collision system (BCI) reports a fault. Nissan issued a bulletin to replace the switch on 2017-2019 models.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin NTB20-065. The switch itself is cheap. Pressing the brake firmly a few times can get you started in a pinch, but have it replaced.

issues.t: 7-speed automatic harsh shifts and hesitation
issues.sym: A thump on downshifts, engine speed wandering at a steady cruise, hesitation when pulling away gently, or a delay when shifting into Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: Shift control software on the 7-speed automatic can cause rough shifts, and a worn valve body (the part that routes fluid to the clutches) causes the same symptoms when the software update does not help.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition, then ask a dealer for any transmission software updates. If the problem stays, ask about valve body repair before agreeing to a full transmission replacement.

issues.t: Rear A/C lines leak under the truck
issues.sym: The rear air conditioning blows warm or only cool air, and the front A/C weakens as refrigerant leaks out.
issues.why: The long metal refrigerant lines that run under the body to the rear A/C unit corrode from road salt and water and start to leak.
issues.next: Have the system dye-tested to find the leak. Patches rarely last; replacing the corroded line section is the lasting fix.

issues.t: Rear self-leveling suspension sags
issues.sym: The rear end sits low, especially after sitting overnight or when towing, the compressor runs a lot, or a suspension warning appears.
issues.why: On trims with rear self-leveling suspension, the air springs leak, the compressor wears out or a ride height sensor fails, so the system cannot hold the rear up.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks before replacing the compressor. Many owners of older trucks convert to regular springs and shocks for a lower long-term cost.

issues.t: Front brake rotors warp early
issues.sym: A pulsing brake pedal or a shaking steering wheel when braking from highway speed, sometimes by 15,000 to 25,000 miles.
issues.why: This is a heavy SUV, and towing or long downhill braking heats the front rotors. Nissan has published service information about the 2017 front rotors.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and replaced with the pads. Quality or upgraded rotors can last longer if you tow.

issues.t: Power liftgate stops working
issues.sym: The liftgate motor whirs but the gate does not move, the gate stops part way and beeps, or it drifts shut.
issues.why: The bolt that connects the liftgate motor to its arm works loose, and the gas struts that hold the gate up wear out.
issues.next: Have the motor-arm bolt checked and tightened with thread locker, and replace both struts as a pair. A new motor is often not needed.

issues.t: Key fob battery drains quickly
issues.sym: A "key battery low" or "no key detected" message, push-button start that does not recognize the fob, or a fob battery that dies within months.
issues.why: Nissan issued bulletins for the Intelligent Key battery discharging early on 2017-2021 Armadas.
issues.next: Replace the fob battery and ask a dealer about the Intelligent Key bulletin. Hold the fob against the start button to start if it is not detected.

issues.t: Emergency braking warning light comes on
issues.sym: The automatic emergency braking (AEB) warning light blinks or stays on and the system switches off, or owners report the truck braking without a reason.
issues.why: Nissan published several bulletins for blinking AEB warnings on these trucks, tied to the front radar and camera system and its software.
issues.next: Keep the front sensor and windshield area clean, and have a dealer check for AEB bulletins and software updates.

issues.t: Emergency braking warning with Ethernet codes
issues.sym: The automatic emergency braking (AEB) warning appears on the dash and the driver-assist features may switch off.
issues.why: Communication faults between the driver-assist computers set Ethernet circuit codes. Nissan bulletin NTB25-045 reprograms the radar control unit on affected trucks.
issues.next: Have a Nissan dealer check for bulletin NTB25-045. It is a software reprogram, normally covered under warranty.

issues.t: Mirror does not return after tilting down in Reverse
issues.sym: The driver mirror tilts down when you shift into Reverse but does not go back to your saved position (or the other way around).
issues.why: Nissan traced it to the driver main power window switch, which also controls the mirror memory, and replaces that switch.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin NTB25-065. They replace the window switch, not the mirror.

issues.t: Power liftgate opens on its own
issues.sym: The hands-free liftgate opens when you did not ask it to, sometimes when you are several feet from the back of the SUV.
issues.why: Owners report the kick sensor triggering from too far away. No official fix had been published at the time of these reports.
issues.next: Turn off the hands-free liftgate feature in the settings if it keeps happening, and report it to your dealer and to NHTSA.

issues.t: Instrument cluster and center screen go blank
issues.sym: The gauge display and center screen black out while driving, sometimes staying off after a restart.
issues.why: Owners report display blackouts on the new 2025 model. It appears to be an electronics or software fault; Nissan had not published a specific fix in these reports.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have the dealer check for software updates. A blank speedometer is a safety issue, so push for a warranty repair.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, hesitates, stalls while driving, or will not start.
issues.why: The plastic impeller in the fuel pump can swell and bind, stopping the pump. Recall 21V373 covers certain 2020-2021 Armadas.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. A Nissan dealer replaces the fuel pump free.

issues.t: Engine relay can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start, then may work again later.
issues.why: Oxide builds up on the contacts of the engine control relay in the under-hood fuse box, so it loses contact. Recall 10V517.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. The dealer replaces the power distribution relay free.

issues.t: Fuel gauge shows fuel when the tank is empty (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge still shows about a quarter tank when the tank is actually empty, so the truck can run out of fuel. Some never read full or drop to empty early.
issues.why: The fuel level sender in the tank reads wrong. Recall 10V074 reprogrammed and repaired affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Until it is fixed, track your mileage and refuel early.

issues.t: A/C condenser fan motor can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the front of the engine bay, or a cooling fan that stops working.
issues.why: Water can get into the condenser fan motor and corrode it, which can make it overheat and start a fire. Recall 08V284.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If you smell burning, park outside and have it inspected.

issues.t: Front lower control link welds may break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension, wandering steering, or a sudden change in handling.
issues.why: Welds on the lower control link collars may not meet strength specs and can separate. Recall 10V208 covers 2010 trucks built from November 2009 to March 2010, and 10E019 covers older trucks repaired with those replacement links.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the links free.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin can slide out (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose or sloppy, or braking power drops.
issues.why: The pivot pin the brake pedal hangs on may not be formed correctly and can slide, partly disconnecting the pedal. Recall 10V072.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the pedal ever feels loose, do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Driver airbag emblem can break loose (recall)
issues.sym: A cracked Nissan emblem on the steering wheel pad. Otherwise no warning signs.
issues.why: The plastic emblem on the driver airbag cover can crack and fly off when the airbag deploys, striking the driver. Recall 23V067.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the dealer repair it free.

issues.t: Master cylinder can reduce front braking (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft and the truck takes longer to stop.
issues.why: The brake master cylinder can intermittently cut pressure to the front brakes. Recall 13V451 covers trucks built February to May 2013.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If braking feels weak, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator may not work properly or may burst during deployment, sending metal pieces into the cabin. Recall 20V188.
issues.next: Check your VIN now. If the recall is open, get the free inflator replacement as soon as possible.

issues.t: Truck may roll while in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The truck creeps or rolls even though the shifter is in Park.
issues.why: The parking pawl inside the transmission may not fully engage because of interference with the housing. Recall 14V803.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Front seat belt may not latch or release (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belt will not click in, or will not release when the button is pressed.
issues.why: Certain front buckles built April to June 2015 may not latch or release properly. Recall 15V501.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Make sure the belt is truly latched by tugging on it.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be left switched off (recall)
issues.sym: No picture appears on the screen when you shift into Reverse after someone changed the display settings.
issues.why: The camera display settings can be changed so the image is hidden, and the setting is kept. Recall 19V654 adds a software fix.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer update is free and quick.

issues.t: Backup camera may not show at start-up (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank when you shift into Reverse soon after starting.
issues.why: A software error in the infotainment system at start-up can keep the rearview camera image from appearing. Recall 25V821.
issues.next: Check your VIN. The software update is free at a dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Wrong axle weight rating on door label (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you will feel. The sticker in the door jamb lists an axle weight rating that is too high on trucks with 22-inch wheels.
issues.why: The certification label shows an incorrect Gross Axle Weight Rating, so owners could overload the truck when loading or towing. Recall 26V455.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Nissan supplies a corrected label free. Until then, do not load to the limit on the old label.
